<ticket source="">
# # Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

- Ticket: request
- State: open

## Description

# Creating a task without a title answers a 500 with a database error

**Type:** bug / error message

`POST /api/tasks` with `{}` answers `500` and `{"error": "Provided value cannot be bound to SQLite parameter 1."}`. With `{"title": ""}` it creates an empty task. A body that is not JSON also answers a 500 with the parser's message. On the page, adding an empty task does nothing visible.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `POST /api/tasks` with a missing, empty or blank (only spaces) `title`, or a `title` that is not a string, answers `400` with `{"error": "title is required"}`, and no task is created.
2. The same rule applies to `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` when the body has a `title`.
3. A title longer than 200 characters (after trimming) answers `400` with `{"error": "title must be at most 200 characters"}`. Titles are saved trimmed.
4. A request body that is not valid JSON answers `400` with `{"error": "invalid JSON body"}`.
5. An unexpected error answers `500` with `{"error": "internal error"}` and never shows the internal message to the client (log it on the server instead).
6. When adding a task fails, the page shows the error message from the API.
7. Tests cover these cases.
</ticket>

plan.summary:
Small bug fix, one task. Today `POST /api/tasks` with `{}` reaches SQLite and answers 500 with the driver message. An empty title creates an empty task. Invalid JSON answers 500 with the parser message. The page's add-task submit handler has no error handling, so a failure does nothing visible.

Plan: one `back` task owns every file, so there is no conflict between tasks. It covers the front-end catch handler too, which is a few lines in `public/app.js`. A separate qa, ux or front task would cost more than the change. The developer writes the tests.

Decisions taken, as the triage step ruled:
- Add one title validator, used by POST and by PATCH when `title` is present. Any non-string, missing, empty or blank title gives 400 `title is required`. This includes `null` on PATCH. After trimming, more than 200 characters gives 400 `title must be at most 200 characters`. The trimmed title is the one saved.
- A body that is invalid JSON, or valid JSON that is not an object (`null`, an array, a number), gives 400 `invalid JSON body`. An empty body stays `{}`, so a missing title then gives `title is required`.
- Typed errors carry their status. Anything else is logged with `console.error` and answers 500 `internal error`. The catch handler in `createServer` must not send the raw message, and must not write if headers were already sent.
- Validate before looking up the task on PATCH, so a bad body gives 400 even for an unknown id.
- On the page, the submit handler catches the failure and calls `show(err)`, which fills the existing `#error` element (`role="alert"`). The form is not reset when the add fails.
- The README's error section is updated, since public behaviour changes.

No question blocks the work. The acceptance criteria are complete and testable.

acceptance.text: POST /api/tasks with a missing, empty, blank (only spaces) or non-string title answers 400 {"error":"title is required"} and no task is created.
PATCH /api/tasks/:id applies the same title rule when the body has a title.
A title longer than 200 characters after trimming answers 400 {"error":"title must be at most 200 characters"}; titles are saved trimmed (POST and PATCH).
A request body that is not valid JSON answers 400 {"error":"invalid JSON body"}.
An unexpected error answers 500 {"error":"internal error"}, never exposes the internal message to the client, and is logged on the server.
When adding a task fails, the page shows the error message from the API in the #error element.

Changing the database schema (no length or NOT NULL constraint)
Authentication, rate limiting or request size limits

tasks.goal:
Fix title validation and error handling end to end. Node 22 with `.ts` imports and no type-checking step; tests run with `npm test` (node:test, `test/tasks.test.ts` starts `createServer()` on port 0 and uses its `call(method, path, body)` helper).

1) `src/tasks.ts`: add an exported `HttpError` class (status number + message) and an exported `parseTitle(value: unknown): string`. It throws `HttpError(400, "title is required")` when the value is not a string or `value.trim()` is empty. It throws `HttpError(400, "title must be at most 200 characters")` when the trimmed string's `.length` is over 200. It returns the trimmed title. `createTask` takes an already-validated title (or calls `parseTitle` itself). `updateTask` must save a trimmed title.

2) `src/app.ts`:
- `readJson` must throw `HttpError(400, "invalid JSON body")` when `JSON.parse` fails. It must also throw it when the parsed value is not a plain object, so `null`, an array, a number or a string are rejected. An empty body stays `{}`.
- POST: `tasks.createTask(db, parseTitle(body.title))`, so a missing title gives 400 `title is required`.
- PATCH: call `parseTitle` only when `"title" in body`, so `{title:null}` is 400 `title is required`, while `{done:true}` still works. Validate before the task lookup. Pass the trimmed title to `updateTask`.
- The catch in `createServer`: an `HttpError` answers its status with `{error: message}`. Anything else is logged with `console.error(err)` and answers 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`. Never send `err.message` of other errors. If `res.headersSent`, just end the response. Keep the `send` helper and the JSON shape `{ "error": "<message>" }`.

3) `public/app.js`: the submit handler (bottom of the file) currently has no error handling. Wrap the `api("/api/tasks", { method: "POST", ... })` and the `form.reset()` / `render()` calls in try/catch and call the existing `show(err)` on failure, so the API's message (e.g. `title is required`) appears in the `#error` element (`role="alert"`). Do not reset the form on failure. Keep the existing style and `api()` helper; do not touch `public/index.html` unless needed.

4) `test/tasks.test.ts`: add tests through the HTTP server for these cases.
- POST with `{}`, `{title:""}`, `{title:"   "}`, `{title:123}` and `{title:null}` each gives 400 `title is required`, and the list length is unchanged.
- POST with a 201-character title gives 400 with the length message. A 200-character title is accepted. `"  padded  "` is saved as `"padded"`.
- PATCH with a blank title gives 400 and the task is unchanged. PATCH with a too-long title gives 400. PATCH with `"  new  "` saves `"new"`. PATCH with only `{done:true}` still works.
- A raw invalid body such as `{nope` sent with `fetch` (the `call` helper only sends valid JSON, so add a raw helper) gives 400 `invalid JSON body`. A body of `null` or `[]` gives the same.
- For 500 masking, force an unexpected error. For example, close the database through a server created in the test, or have the test throw inside the path. Assert 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`, that the body does not contain the internal message, and that `console.error` was called (mock it with `node:test`'s `mock.method` and restore it).

5) `README.md`: in the API section (around lines 13-23), document the 400 answers for POST and PATCH (`title is required`, `title must be at most 200 characters`, `invalid JSON body`), the trimming, and `500 internal error`.

Run `npm test` and make sure it passes.

Ruling: skip the product owner (frame) — the ticket already lists 7 testable acceptance criteria covering POST, PATCH, length limit, invalid JSON, 500 masking and the page error — cost if wrong: an edge case such as `title: null` on PATCH or a non-object JSON body is left to the developer; treat any non-string title as 'title is required' (400) and a JSON body that is not an object as 'invalid JSON body'.

Ruling: no PM, architect, UX or SEO steps — no vague scope, no cross-cutting decision, the page only shows an existing error element (#error, show() in public/app.js), no public-page metadata change — cost if wrong: none expected.

Ruling: size S, a single back-end task plus the front-end catch handler, with tests written by the same developers, no separate qa task — cost if wrong: a missed criterion caught later by the code review.

Ruling: security review at medium effort — the change touches input parsing and error disclosure (criterion 5: no internal message to the client) but adds no authentication, payment or personal data — cost if wrong: a leak path such as an error raised before the catch handler goes unnoticed.

Ruling: budget $0.80 — covers one small implement round, the checks, a code review round with one fix pass, the medium security review and the visual review — cost if wrong: the run stops before its reviews and the user must approve more.

reviews.summary:
I found no bugs and every acceptance criterion is met. I read the whole diff (src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts, public/app.js, README.md, test/tasks.test.ts) and ran `npm test`. All 12 tests pass.

- **AC1–AC3:** `parseTitle` rejects missing, non-string, blank and null titles with 400 `title is required`. It rejects a trimmed title over 200 characters with the length message, and it returns the trimmed title. POST and PATCH both use it. PATCH validates when `"title" in body`, before the task lookup, so `{title:null}` gives 400 and `{done:true}` still works.
- **AC4:** `readJson` answers 400 `invalid JSON body` for unparseable bodies and for JSON that is not an object (`null`, an array, a number). An empty body stays `{}`.
- **AC5:** the `createServer` catch handler answers a known `HttpError` with its own status and message. Anything else goes to `console.error` and answers 500 `internal error`. If headers were already sent, it only ends the response.
- **AC6:** the submit handler in `public/app.js` catches the failure and calls `show(err)`. `api()` throws `Error(body.error)`, so the API message reaches `#error`. The form is not reset when the add fails. I did not run this in a browser, and the implementer did not either. No browser test exists in the project.
- **AC7:** the tests cover each case through the real HTTP server. The 500 test mocks `DatabaseSync.prototype.prepare`, then checks the masked body and the `console.error` call. They would fail without the feature. One small gap: no test shows that PATCH with a bad body on an unknown id gives 400 instead of 404. The code does this correctly.

One nit: the title is validated twice. I did not review security beyond the criteria, and I did not run a typecheck, because the project has none.

findings.scenario: POST calls `parseTitle(body.title)` in the route and `createTask` calls `parseTitle` again. PATCH does the same through `updateTask`. The second call is a harmless no-op because `parseTitle` is idempotent, but the two layers show two places where validation can happen.
findings.fix: Keep validation in one layer. Either have the route pass the raw value and let `createTask` and `updateTask` validate, or have `createTask` and `updateTask` take an already-parsed string. If it stays in `updateTask`, the route still needs the pre-lookup validation for the unknown-id case.

report.summary:
Title validation and error handling now work end to end. `npm test` passes (12 tests, 7 of them new). I did not run a typecheck, because the project has none, and I did not open the page in a browser.

- **`src/tasks.ts`:** new `HttpError` (status and message) and `parseTitle`. `parseTitle` throws 400 `title is required` for a non-string or blank title, and 400 `title must be at most 200 characters` when the trimmed title is over 200. It returns the trimmed title. `createTask` and `updateTask` both call it, so titles are saved trimmed.
- **`src/app.ts`:**
  - `readJson` throws 400 `invalid JSON body` for bad JSON and for JSON that is not a plain object (`null`, an array, a number or a string). An empty body is still `{}`.
  - POST validates `body.title`. PATCH validates only when `"title" in body`, before the task lookup, so `{title:null}` is 400 and `{done:true}` still works.
  - The `createServer` catch answers an `HttpError` with its status and message. Anything else goes to `console.error` and answers 500 `internal error`, with no raw message. If headers were already sent, it only ends the response.
- **`public/app.js`:** the submit handler wraps the POST, `form.reset()` and `render()` in try/catch and calls `show(err)`. The API message shows in `#error`, and the form is not reset on failure.
- **`README.md`:** documents the 400 answers, the trimming, the invalid JSON case and the 500 `internal error`.
- **Tests (`test/tasks.test.ts`):**
  - Blank, missing, `null` and numeric titles on POST give 400, and the list length is unchanged.
  - The 200 and 201 character limit on POST, and trimming.
  - PATCH with a blank, `null`, numeric or too-long title gives 400 and leaves the task unchanged. PATCH with `"  new  "` saves `"new"`, and `{done:true}` still works.
  - Invalid JSON, `null`, `[]` and `5` give 400 on POST and PATCH.
  - 500 masking: I mock `DatabaseSync.prototype.prepare` to throw, then check the 500 body, that the secret text is absent, and that `console.error` was called with it.

The page's error display (AC6) has no automated test, since the project has no browser test setup.

report.summary:
No vulnerability confirmed in the run's changes. I read the full diff of src/app.ts, src/tasks.ts and public/app.js, plus the page's error display code. I did not run the tests or an audit.

Checked and found sound:
- A10:2025 (errors that fail open or leak): the catch handler in createServer answers only HttpError messages, which are fixed strings. Any other error goes to console.error and the client gets "internal error". If headers were already sent it only ends the response, so it cannot throw a second time. No path I found sends a raw driver or parser message.
- A05:2025 (injection): SQL still uses bound parameters. The title is now always a trimmed string before it reaches SQLite, so the driver error that leaked a message is gone. `done` is only used as a truthy test, so a wrong type cannot reach the database as a bad value.
- XSS: the page writes the API error with textContent, and task titles with textContent, so a title or error text cannot inject HTML.
- Input parsing: readJson rejects bad JSON and bodies that are not objects with a fixed message. `"title" in body` is safe because body is a plain object. Validation runs before the task lookup on PATCH, so a bad body gives 400 even for an unknown id. That is not an enumeration risk.
- A03:2025 (dependencies): no package was added. package.json has no dependencies.

Hardening notes, not findings (all explicitly out of scope in the ticket):
- readJson has no body size limit, so one large request can use memory. The limit was not set before this change either.
- A request error raised after the body stream breaks is not specially handled. This existed before the change.
- The title is validated twice (in app.ts and again in tasks.ts). That is harmless.

Not covered: runtime testing, a dependency audit (there are no dependencies), the authentication model (the app has none), and the browser behaviour of the page.
out_of_scope_findings: No request body size limit in readJson (src/app.ts): a very large body is buffered in memory. Existed before the change; the ticket puts request size limits out of scope.
The API has no authentication or rate limiting; the ticket puts both out of scope.
